mainPoints.explanation: Workforce reduced from 120,000 to 83,000, saving nearly $10 billion annually in costs; already profitable under non-GAAP measures; the layoffs have shown immediate results.
mainPoints.point: Lip-Bu Tan rapidly improved Intel's financial situation through aggressive layoffs and cost control.

mainPoints.explanation: Through private placements to the U.S. government, NVIDIA, SoftBank, and others, as well as the sale of its memory business, Intel secured ample cash to support fab construction and technology R&D.
mainPoints.point: Equity restructuring and asset divestitures injected $21.1 billion in "lifesaving" funds for Intel, averting bankruptcy risk.

mainPoints.explanation: Yield has improved from a low point to 60%-80%, confirmed by third-party analysts; internal orders (Core Ultra, Xeon 6+) have passed verification, but insufficient capacity remains a major constraint.
mainPoints.point: The continuous yield breakthrough of the 18A process is key to Intel's foundry business turnaround.

mainPoints.explanation: Agents rely on CPUs for context switching when calling external tools, with the CPU:GPU ratio adjusting from 1:8 to 1:1; Intel's client and data center businesses are expected to benefit continuously.
mainPoints.point: The structural growth in CPU demand from AI Agents provides a new market narrative for Intel.

oneSentenceSummary: This article provides an in-depth analysis of Intel CEO Lip-Bu Tan's reform strategies over the 14 months since he took office, including layoffs, equity restructuring, betting on the 18A process, and explores the positive impact of AI Agents on CPU demand, looking ahead to the prospect of a trillion-dollar market cap.
originalTitle: 英特尔，10000 亿市值还有多远？
summary: The article revolves around Intel CEO Lip-Bu Tan's "corrective" actions since taking the helm, systematically summarizing four core measures: cutting 30% of the workforce to save nearly $10 billion annually; securing a $15.9 billion equity restructuring involving external capital from the U.S. government, NVIDIA, SoftBank, etc., and divesting non-core assets to raise $5.2 billion, resolving the liquidity crisis; navigating between politics and business under external pressure, delaying some fab construction and emphasizing "America First"; and pushing forward the 18A process yield ramp-up, which has now exceeded 60% and even approached 80%, applied to Core Ultra and Xeon 6+ platforms. The article further points out that AI Agents' increasing reliance on CPUs (with the CPU:GPU ratio adjusting from 1:8 to 1:1) brings a new growth narrative for Intel, but capacity bottlenecks and external uncertainties remain challenges. Overall, this is an information-dense, logically coherent in-depth analysis with both business and technology perspectives.
title: Intel: How Far from a Trillion-Dollar Market Cap?
